newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-PASSARELLA FACES ANOTHER ALTITUDE PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PASSARELLA FACES ANOTHER ALTITUDE PROBLEM.

text.p: Argentina coach Daniel Passarella faced another altitude problem Thursday after reports that Chile might play their World Cup qualifier at home to Argentina in the city of Calama at 2,600 metres above sea level.
"I haven't heard anything about this, but if it is the case then it appears we are the ugly ducklings," he said. "We would be the only ones to play there."
Chile have played all their World Cup matches so far in the capital Santiago, which is at sea level and where ironically they have a perfect percent record. They face Argentina in September.
Altitude is a question that has haunted Passarella all year.

In April, his team were beaten 2-1 away by Bolivia in a World Cup qualifier played in La Paz at 3,600 metres above sea level. Passarella got a hot reception in the city after inflaming local passions with a declaration that it was "inhuman" to make players perform at such a height.
On the eve of the match, he walked out of a news conference following a row with a local about the remark.

This week, he threatened to pull Argentina out of the Copa America in the same country following a rule change which would have switched their quarter-final to La Paz if the game had been against Bolivia.
Bolivia averted the crisis by winning their group, meaning that Argentina will play Peru instead in the originally planned venue of Sucre.
